grid.method: fixed equirectangular grid classified by cell center

sources.name: DeepStateMap public history
sources.role: Dated territorial-control snapshots used to classify grid-cell transitions

sources.name: Russian Casualties in Ukraine API
sources.role: Daily reported Russian personnel-loss increments aggregated by calendar month

sources.name: Ukraine Common Operational Dataset administrative boundaries
sources.role: 2022 ADM0 land boundary used to keep grid-cell centers inside internationally recognized Ukraine

methodology: A deterministic approximately 10 x 10 km grid is clipped to the OCHA Ukraine ADM0 land boundary and classified by cell center against each archived control snapshot. Polygon and MultiPolygon members nested in GeoJSON GeometryCollection features inherit their parent metadata and are included. Transnistria is retained only as map context and is excluded from both the Ukraine grid and snapshot occupation classification. Every observed Ukrainian change of control receives a modeled calendar month. Reported personnel losses are divided by gross changed area (Russian gains plus Ukrainian liberations, never signed net area) and allocated equally by modeled changed area across all transition events in that month.
confidence_method: Transitions observed between snapshots in the same month use that month. A transition ending on day 1 or 2 of the next month is assigned to the preceding month. Other cross-month transitions are deterministically distributed inside their observed interval by a stable cell-and-interval hash and are labeled interpolated_interval; this models a month without claiming an observed change date.
limitation: This is a spatial and temporal allocation model, not a record of deaths at a location or an observed date of control change. Personnel values are reported or claimed, are not independently verified here, and include the upstream personnel-loss definition. Cross-month interpolation, cell-center classification, sparse snapshots, source-boundary revisions, and equal 100 km2 cells introduce uncertainty. Pre-2022 occupied Crimea and Donbas cells are context only and receive no full-scale-war allocation; Transnistria and any overlap caused by differing source borders are excluded.
